maria_sales: Quick sync re: Zephyr customer (RK Labs). They asked whether we can be a drop-in for their existing integration — they currently hit Zephyr's /v1/generate and rely on specific JSON fields. Can we map responses without a full prompt rewrite?

dan_engineer: short answer: yes, with caveats. We can offer an adapter proxy that rewrites requests + normalizes responses. but differences in tokenization and default stop sequences will cause subtle output shifts.

olivia_se: +1. Example mapping we did for a proof-of-concept: proxy replaces Zephyr header X-Zephyr-Key -> Authorization: Bearer <key> and remaps body from { "prompt": "..." } -> { "input": "..." } then post-processes result to add Zephyr-style "choices" array.

olivia_se: code sample we plan to hand them for the POC (curl):

```bash
curl -X POST https://proxy.redwood.local/zephyr-compat \
  -H 'X-Zephyr-Key: <key>' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the doc"}'
# proxy does: 1) header -> Authorization 2) body key rename 3) call Redwood /v1/generate 4) wrap response as Zephyr-style JSON
```

maria_sales: Good — they specifically care about these items in the presales convo: 1) prompt parity (we need examples showing same output 90%+), 2) pricing delta for token accounting differences, 3) security questionnaire answers for data residency + retention.

dan_engineer: On prompt parity: we should run a side-by-side eval suite of 300 prompts (mix of instruction, chat, and long-context). We'll capture BLEU/ROUGE + human pass/fail for critical prompts. We should also include cases where Zephyr relied on a particular sampling seed behavior. Zephyr seeds were deterministic by default for their clients. We can't guarantee exact token-level parity but can match intent/slots.

rk_cto: quick Q from their infra team: embeddings from Zephyr are 768-dim, ours are 1024-dim for the model they want. That breaks their vector DB schema. Can you offer a fallback?

dan_engineer: two options: 1) provide a quantized dim-reduction shim (PCA on-server) that returns 768 vectors — extra latency ~15-35ms; 2) we can onboard their vector DB to accept 1024 dims and provide migration scripts. For POC, option 1 is faster.

janelle_security: Security items they flagged in questionnaire: SOC2 attestation, KMS integration, VPC peering, tenant isolation guarantees, ability to delete logs on demand. We have templated answers but need to confirm data-at-rest encryption key scope for redwood-private.

olivia_se: I'll attach the templated answers in the deck, but for the public hosted flow we cannot promise deletion of aggregated telemetry for compliance customers — we do provide retention controls and export options. For Dedicated/Private we can meet delete-on-request and customer KMS.

maria_sales: Pricing question — they quoted Zephyr at $0.0008/token for gen and $0.002/embedding. RK is asking for parity or a migration credit for the first 6 months. Thoughts?

dan_engineer: We should model unit economics. If we enable the PCA shim, there's infra cost but it's small. Recommend offering a tiered credit: 3 months 50% credit, 3 months 25% credit for hosted API until they've validated parity. If they buy Dedicated we can negotiate a committed discount.

rk_cto: They also run a high-rate burst profile (500 rps sustained for 2 minutes) during nightly processing windows. Zephyr allowed 1k rps burst on their plan. Can Redwood match?

olivia_se: For POC we can provision a small burst pool on Dedicated preview; for hosted we'll route through our burst-capacity fallback but we'd need to bump their rate limit during the test window. Need approvals from infra.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: created branch zephyr-compat/proxy-2026-03-18, can spin up a staging proxy with env var ENABLE_PCA=true.

maria_sales: Action items:
- olivia: assemble presales package + questionnaire answers (deadline: 2026-03-22)
- dan: run 300-prompt parity run, include seed/determinism tests + embedding dim conversion latency (deadline: 2026-03-24)
- janelle: provide clarified data residency + KMS language and confirm whether Hosted can offer log deletion for this customer (deadline: 2026-03-21)
- ops: provision proxy staging for RK test window (target date: 2026-03-25)

janelle_security: Note: I'll escalate hosted log deletion question to legal — host offering is usually retention controls only. If they require deletion by policy, recommend Dedicated or Private.

rk_cto: Thanks — this looks promising. Can we also get a short runbook for rollback if outputs diverge in prod? Last thing their engineers want is silent behavior changes after cutover.

dan_engineer: We'll include automatic canary: 10% traffic to Redwood + parallel comparison to Zephyr for 48 hours, auto-failover if semantic drift (as measured by our eval heuristics) crosses threshold. We'll produce the rollback runbook doc.

maria_sales: Nice. I'll draft the customer email with timeline after we get the presales deck.

olivia_se: Also flag: Zephyr supports a custom field "trace_id" echoed back in responses; our proxy will preserve it if present so their logs remain stable.

rk_cto: Perfect. pls cc my infra lead: infra-ryan@rklabs.com on the deck and runbook.

maria_sales: will do. thanks everyone :rocket:
